answers.ui_testing: Headless Chromium via Playwright (pre-installed in the environment): render the real single-page app — Leaflet map included, with map tiles and other network faked deterministically — and assert pixel-exact visual goldens the owner reviews by sight; short per-leaf tests drive to a state and capture. Pure planner rules (plan/lib) stay node --test logic leaves. No visual harness exists yet — this is the target mechanism.
answers.requirements_source: Authored fresh at product/requirements.md (config.spec), distilled from the existing product brief docs/product-spec.md. No prior formal requirements doc or issue-tracker backlog to extract.

answers.product: Fringe Discover: a spontaneity/reachability tool for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. Where listings apps answer 'what exists?', this answers 'what can I actually make right now?' — given the user's location, how far they'll travel and how, and their next commitment, it collapses ~3,800 shows into a short list of genuinely reachable options that haven't started and still leave time to reach whatever is next.
answers.users: Fringe-goers mid-festival, usually on foot and without a fixed plan — visitors with a gap between a booked show and dinner, locals and tourists intimidated by the programme's scale. Decisive in the moment rather than researchers: they want a short list of good, reachable options, not 3,800 search results. Emotional target: 'delight + relief'.
answers.market: Edinburgh Fringe discovery and planning tools. Alternatives: the official Fringe app (a 'Nearby now' + shake-to-search finder), Plan My Fringe (a schedule optimiser with a walking-time 'Fringe Trail'), the edfringe.com programme and filters, the Half Price Hut (same-day discounts), review outlets such as ThreeWeeks, plus street posters and word-of-mouth. None centres full reachability — travel mode plus next-commitment slack — the way Fringe Discover does.

answers.hosting: GitHub Pages, from this repo — the existing pages.yml is an artifact-flow Pages deploy of the repo root, so the full release-on-push → Pages pipeline applies.
answers.publish_set: The site is served from the repo root: .nojekyll, the four pages (index, accessibility, privacy, terms), css/, js/, shared/, data/, package.json (the debug pill fetches it for the version), and the planner front-end (plan/index.html, plan.css, plan.js, lib/). The trees that MAKE the site — scraper/, docs/, design-concepts/, plan/design/, product-wiki/, scripts/ — were served by the old whole-root upload and are deliberately not published.
